text.en: What is the build output of a SQL Database Project?
A .dacpac file
A .bacpac file
A .bak backup
A .mdf data file

explanation.en: Building produces a .dacpac — a schema model used for deployment. A .bacpac contains schema plus data (export/import), .bak is a backup, .mdf a data file.

example.en: dotnet build → bin/Debug/MyDb.dacpac

text.en: Which MSBuild SDK defines SDK-style SQL projects?
Microsoft.Build.Sql
Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web
Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore
System.Data.SqlClient

explanation.en: Microsoft.Build.Sql is the SDK for modern SQL projects (cross-platform, dotnet build). The others are web SDK, ORM and a driver.

example.en: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.Build.Sql/1.0.0"> … </Project>

text.en: Which three are advantages of SDK-style SQL projects over original SQL projects? (Select 3)
Cross-platform builds with .NET 8+
NuGet package references for database references
Default globbing of .sql files (no per-file entries in the project file)
They require a live database to build
They only work in Visual Studio

explanation.en: SDK-style projects build anywhere with dotnet, support package references and include .sql files automatically. They don't need a live database, and they're the format used by VS Code and Fabric source control.

example.en: Globbing reduces merge conflicts in the .sqlproj file.

text.en: A project uses JSON_OBJECT and builds fail with errors about unsupported syntax. The project's target platform is SQL Server 2017 (Sql140). What should you change?
Set the target platform (DSP) to the actual target, e.g. Azure SQL Database or SQL Server 2025
Disable the build
Rename the files to .txt
Add NOLOCK

explanation.en: Build validates syntax against the target platform; newer functions fail on older targets. Align the DSP with where you deploy.

example.en: <DSP>Microsoft.Data.Tools.Schema.Sql.SqlAzureV12DatabaseSchemaProvider</DSP>

text.en: A view in the project references a column that doesn't exist in the table definition. What happens at build time?
The build fails with an unresolved reference error
The build succeeds; the error appears only at runtime
The column is created automatically
The view is silently skipped

explanation.en: Reference validation is a core benefit of SQL projects: broken dependencies are caught at build time, long before deployment.

example.en: SQL71501: View [dbo].[vOrders] has an unresolved reference to object [dbo].[Orders].[Discount].

text.en: Match each SqlPackage action to its purpose.
Publish
Script
DeployReport
Extract
Apply the dacpac's schema to a target database
Generate the T-SQL deployment script without running it
Produce an XML report of changes a publish would make
Create a dacpac from an existing database

explanation.en: These four actions cover the deploy lifecycle; DriftReport (not listed) reports schema changes made outside deployments.

example.en: Generate Script for review in a PR, then Publish after approval.

text.en: A deployment would drop a column containing data. With default publish settings, what happens?
The publish is blocked because BlockOnPossibleDataLoss is true by default
The column is dropped silently
The data is moved to a backup table automatically
The deployment ignores the change

explanation.en: BlockOnPossibleDataLoss defaults to true, stopping deployments that might lose data. You can override it deliberately in a publish profile after handling data migration.

example.en: Migrate data in a pre-deployment script first, then allow the change.

text.en: How should static lookup data (e.g. OrderStatus rows) be managed in a SQL project?
Idempotent MERGE statements in the post-deployment script, stored in source control
Manually inserted after each deployment
INSERT statements in the table's CREATE file
Stored only in production

explanation.en: Post-deployment MERGE converges lookup tables to the versioned set on every deployment without duplicates. Manual steps drift; table files must contain only the declarative definition.

example.en: MERGE dbo.OrderStatus USING (VALUES …) AS src … WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN INSERT …

text.en: For each statement about pre/post-deployment scripts, answer Yes or No.
A project can have only one pre-deployment and one post-deployment script.
Other script files can be included with the SQLCMD :r command.
Post-deployment scripts run only on the first deployment.

explanation.en: There's one of each, organized via :r includes. They run on every deployment, which is why they must be idempotent.

example.en: :r .\ReferenceData\OrderStatus.sql

text.en: Why are SQL projects described as 'declarative'?
Each object is defined once in its desired final state; the deployment engine computes the ALTER steps
They declare variables only
They store a numbered list of migration scripts
They can't change existing databases

explanation.en: You edit CREATE definitions; DacFx compares model vs target and generates the changes. Migration-based tools (option c) are the alternative approach.

example.en: Add a column to the CREATE TABLE file → deployment generates ALTER TABLE … ADD.

text.en: Complete the commands to build a project and generate a reviewable deployment script.
build
run
publish-db
Script
Export
Import

explanation.en: dotnet build creates the dacpac; SqlPackage Script writes the change script for review. Export/Import work with bacpacs (schema + data).

example.en: Attach deploy.sql as a pipeline artifact for approvers.

text.en: Your procedure references sys.objects-style objects from master and the build reports unresolved references. What's the SDK-style fix?
Add a NuGet package reference to the master system dacpac (e.g. Microsoft.SqlServer.Dacpacs.Master)
Copy master's tables into the project
Disable validation globally
Change the file encoding

explanation.en: System database references resolve external objects. SDK-style projects reference them as packages. Copying system objects or disabling validation are wrong.

example.en: <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.SqlServer.Dacpacs.Master" Version="…" />

text.en: A procedure queries another database whose name differs per environment (SalesDev, SalesProd). How should the project reference it?
A database reference with a SQLCMD variable, used as [$(SalesDb)].dbo.Orders
Hard-code SalesProd everywhere
Use dynamic SQL for every query
It isn't possible

explanation.en: SQLCMD variables let the publish profile supply the right database name per environment while keeping references validated.

example.en: Publish profile: <SqlCmdVariable Include="SalesDb"><Value>SalesProd</Value></SqlCmdVariable>

text.en: Order the lifecycle of a schema change in a SQL project workflow.
Edit the object's CREATE definition file
Build the project (validation → .dacpac)
Generate a script/DeployReport against the target for review
Publish the .dacpac to the target

explanation.en: Edit declaratively, validate by building, review the computed changes, then publish.

example.en: CI runs steps 2–3 on every pull request.

text.en: How do you start a SQL project from an existing production database?
Extract the schema (SqlPackage /Action:Extract or 'Create project from database' in tools) into a project
Copy the .mdf file into the repository
Back up the database to Git
Write every CREATE statement by hand

explanation.en: Extract generates a dacpac (and tools can create .sql files per object) from a live database. Data files and backups aren't source code.

example.en: sqlpackage /Action:Extract /SourceConnectionString:"…" /TargetFile:prod.dacpac /p:ExtractTarget=SchemaObjectType

text.en: Which tool provides the GA authoring experience for SDK-style SQL projects?
The SQL Database Projects extension for Visual Studio Code
Notepad
Excel
SQL Server Configuration Manager

explanation.en: SDK-style projects are GA in VS Code (and in preview in Visual Studio 2022); the CLI also works. The other tools aren't project authoring environments.

example.en: VS Code: 'Create Project from Database', build, publish, schema compare.

text.en: For each statement about the .dacpac, answer Yes or No.
One dacpac can be published to many databases (e.g. a fleet of tenants).
A dacpac contains all table data.
Publishing to a new database creates objects in dependency order.

explanation.en: A dacpac is a schema model (plus pre/post scripts), reusable across targets; data travels in bacpacs. DacFx orders object creation by dependencies (e.g. referenced tables first).

example.en: Loop sqlpackage /Action:Publish over 100 tenant databases.

text.en: What does setting DropObjectsNotInSource = true in a publish profile do?
Drops objects in the target that don't exist in the dacpac
Drops all data
Drops the database before deploying
Prevents any drop

explanation.en: It makes the target exactly match the project by removing extra objects — powerful for drift cleanup, dangerous if other teams create objects in the same database. Use exclusion options when needed.

example.en: Combine with DoNotDropObjectTypes to protect users/permissions.

text.en: Where are environment-specific deployment settings (target connection, SQLCMD variable values, options) best stored?
Publish profiles (*.publish.xml), with secrets supplied by the pipeline
Inside each table's CREATE script
In the .dacpac name
In the post-deployment script

explanation.en: Publish profiles hold per-environment options; credentials should come from secrets/identity, not the profile file. Object definitions and scripts shouldn't contain environment config.

example.en: dev.publish.xml, test.publish.xml, prod.publish.xml

text.en: Which property enables static code analysis rules (such as avoiding SELECT *) during build?
RunSqlCodeAnalysis
TreatWarningsAsErrors only
EnableQueryStore
BlockOnPossibleDataLoss

explanation.en: RunSqlCodeAnalysis turns on DacFx code analysis. Rules can be configured as warnings or errors. The other properties do different things.

example.en: <RunSqlCodeAnalysis>true</RunSqlCodeAnalysis>

text.en: Which two belong in a SQL project as declarative object files? (Select 2)
CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders (…)
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.GetOrders …
ALTER TABLE dbo.Orders ADD Discount … (as a standalone change script)
DROP TABLE dbo.OldOrders

explanation.en: Projects contain CREATE definitions of the desired state. ALTER/DROP change scripts belong to migration-based workflows; in a project you edit/remove the definition and the deployment generates the changes.

example.en: To drop OldOrders, delete its file (and enable DropObjectsNotInSource if desired).

text.en: A column rename in the project file deploys as DROP column + ADD column, losing data. How do you make the deployment perform a rename?
Use the tool's rename refactoring so a refactor log records the rename, which the deployment turns into sp_rename
Turn off BlockOnPossibleDataLoss
Rename the file only
Use NOLOCK

explanation.en: Without intent, the engine sees an old column missing and a new column present. Refactoring records the rename in a refactorlog so publish issues sp_rename and preserves data. Disabling the data-loss block would lose the data.

example.en: The .refactorlog file must be committed with the change.

text.en: Which source control integration in Microsoft Fabric uses the SDK-style SQL project format?
SQL database in Fabric Git integration
Power BI paginated reports
OneLake shortcuts
Fabric capacity metrics

explanation.en: SQL database in Fabric's Git integration stores the database as an SDK-style SQL project, enabling the same build/deploy tooling.

example.en: Commit from the Fabric workspace; the repo contains .sqlproj and .sql files.

text.en: Complete the idempotent reference-data script for the post-deployment step.

questions.code:
[BLANK1] dbo.Currency AS tgt
USING (VALUES ('USD', N'US Dollar'), ('PKR', N'Pakistani Rupee')) AS src (Code, Name)
    ON tgt.Code = src.Code
WHEN MATCHED AND tgt.Name <> src.Name THEN UPDATE SET Name = src.Name
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY [BLANK2] THEN INSERT (Code, Name) VALUES (src.Code, src.Name);

text.en: MERGE
INSERT INTO
TRUNCATE
TARGET
SOURCE
INDEX

explanation.en: MERGE makes the script safe to re-run. 'NOT MATCHED BY TARGET' inserts source rows missing in the table; 'BY SOURCE' would handle rows to delete. INSERT alone would duplicate rows; TRUNCATE breaks foreign keys and history.

example.en: Add WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE to remove retired codes.

text.en: Which command creates a new SDK-style SQL project from the CLI (after installing the templates)?
dotnet new sqlproj -n MyDatabase
sqlcmd -create MyDatabase
npm init sqlproj
git sql init

explanation.en: Install Microsoft.Build.Sql.Templates, then use dotnet new sqlproj. The other commands don't exist for this purpose.

example.en: dotnet new install Microsoft.Build.Sql.Templates

text.en: A team uses EF Core migrations for the app but wants a single source of truth for the full schema, including objects EF doesn't manage. What does Microsoft suggest SQL projects can do?
Track the database state by extracting the schema into a SQL project regardless of the ORM used
Replace EF Core entirely
Only work without ORMs
Store migrations as dacpacs

explanation.en: SQL projects can represent the database's source of truth even when an ORM creates it; schema can be extracted into the project for validation, review and drift detection.

example.en: Extract after each release to keep the declarative model current.

text.en: Match each project artifact to its role.
.sqlproj
.dacpac
.publish.xml
Script.PostDeployment.sql
Project definition: SDK, target platform, references
Build output: the schema model to deploy
Per-environment deployment options
Runs after schema changes (e.g. reference data)

explanation.en: The four core artifacts of the SQL project workflow.

example.en: Only .sqlproj, .sql files and profiles go into Git; the dacpac is a build artifact.

text.en: Should the built .dacpac be committed to the Git repository?
No — it's a build artifact; CI builds it from source and publishes it as a pipeline artifact
Yes, always alongside every commit
Only the production dacpac
Dacpacs can't be stored anywhere

explanation.en: Like compiled binaries, dacpacs are reproducible from source; commit sources, keep build outputs as CI artifacts (or package feeds for referenced dacpacs).

example.en: Add bin/ and obj/ to .gitignore.

text.en: Adding a NOT NULL column without a default to a table that has rows. Answer Yes or No.
The deployment may fail or be blocked because existing rows have no value.
Adding a DEFAULT constraint in the definition lets the deployment populate existing rows.
SqlPackage ignores NOT NULL constraints.

explanation.en: Existing rows need a value; a default (or a pre-deployment data step / smart defaults option) resolves it. SqlPackage respects constraints.

example.en: Discount DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_Orders_Discount DEFAULT (0)

text.en: Which tool compares a project (or dacpac) with a live database and shows differences interactively?
Schema compare
Query Store
Database Engine Tuning Advisor
SQL Server Agent

explanation.en: Schema compare (VS Code, Visual Studio, SqlPackage-based) highlights differences and can update either side. The others are performance or scheduling tools.

example.en: Use it to spot changes made directly in production (drift).

text.en: Your schema includes a vector column and the project build fails on the VECTOR type. What is the most likely issue?
Outdated tooling or a target platform that doesn't support vector — update Microsoft.Build.Sql/DacFx and set a supporting target
Vector columns can never be in projects
The column needs NOLOCK
Vectors must be stored in JSON files

explanation.en: Vector support arrived in recent DacFx/SqlPackage and Microsoft.Build.Sql versions; older tooling or targets fail. Projects support vectors with current tools.

example.en: Docs list Microsoft.Build.Sql 1.0.0+ and SqlPackage 162.5+ as supporting the vector type.

text.en: What's the difference between a .dacpac and a .bacpac?
A dacpac holds schema (for deployments); a bacpac holds schema and data (for export/import/migration)
They're identical
A bacpac is for backups to tape only
A dacpac contains only data

explanation.en: Dacpacs drive schema deployments; bacpacs move whole databases (e.g. Azure SQL export). Neither replaces native backups.

example.en: sqlpackage /Action:Export creates a bacpac.

text.en: Order the steps to safely split a column FullName into FirstName and LastName with a SQL project deployment.
Add FirstName/LastName (nullable) to the table definition
Post-deployment script populates the new columns from FullName (idempotently)
Release apps that use the new columns
Later deployment removes FullName (data already migrated)

explanation.en: Expand → migrate data → switch consumers → contract. Removing FullName in the same release would block on data loss or break running apps.

example.en: The expand/contract pattern keeps deployments backward compatible.

text.en: Why might a team split one large database into several SQL projects referencing each other as 'same database' references?
To let different teams own parts of the schema while composing one database model
To deploy to different servers automatically
Because one project can't contain more than 10 tables
To avoid validation

explanation.en: Same-database references compose multiple projects into one database model with full validation. There's no 10-table limit, and validation remains.

example.en: Core.sqlproj (shared tables) referenced by Billing.sqlproj and Shipping.sqlproj.

text.en: Which two are build-time (not deploy-time) checks? (Select 2)
Unresolved object references
Syntax valid for the target platform
Existing data violating a new constraint in production
Login permissions on the target server

explanation.en: Builds validate the model offline. Data-dependent issues and target permissions surface only when deploying to a real database.

example.en: That's why CI should also deploy to a test database.

text.en: A pre-deployment script inserts rows into a table that is being created in the same deployment. It fails on the first deployment. Why?
Pre-deployment runs BEFORE schema changes, so the table doesn't exist yet — move the insert to post-deployment
Pre-deployment scripts can't contain INSERTs
The table must be temporal
It needs NOLOCK

explanation.en: Execution order: pre-deployment → schema changes → post-deployment. Data for new tables belongs in post-deployment.

example.en: Pre-deployment is for preparing data that a schema change depends on.

text.en: Which library provides the core functionality behind SQL projects, SqlPackage and schema compare?
DacFx (Microsoft.SqlServer.DacFx)
Entity Framework
SignalR
Polly

explanation.en: DacFx builds models, compares schemas and generates deployments; tools surface it. The others are ORM, real-time messaging and resilience libraries.

example.en: DacFx extensibility allows custom deployment contributors and code analysis rules.

text.en: Answer Yes or No about code analysis in SQL projects.
Rules can flag patterns like SELECT * or unused variables.
Rule violations can be configured to fail the build.
Code analysis requires a connection to production.

explanation.en: Code analysis runs offline on the model; severities can be raised to errors to enforce standards in CI.

example.en: <SqlCodeAnalysisRules>+!Microsoft.Rules.Data.SR0001</SqlCodeAnalysisRules> (treat as error)

text.en: Which statement about SQL projects and new vs existing databases is correct?
For new databases objects are created in dependency order; for existing ones only the differences are applied
Existing databases are always dropped and recreated
Projects can only create new databases
Differences must be scripted by hand

explanation.en: Publish handles both: create in correct order, or compute incremental ALTERs. No drop/recreate and no manual diff scripts.

example.en: Missing two columns + changed proc → ALTER TABLE + ALTER PROCEDURE.

text.en: Two developers each add a different .sql file to an SDK-style project. Why do they avoid a merge conflict in the .sqlproj file?
Default globbing includes .sql files automatically, so the project file doesn't change
Git ignores .sqlproj files
SDK-style projects lock the file
They can't add files

explanation.en: Original projects listed every file in the project, so concurrent additions conflicted. Globbing removes that hotspot.

example.en: Exclude files with <Build Remove="Scratch\**" /> if needed.

text.en: Which SqlPackage action reports schema changes made to a registered database since its last deployment?
DriftReport
Import
Extract
Export

explanation.en: DriftReport compares a registered data-tier application with its current state. Import/Export move bacpacs; Extract creates a dacpac.

example.en: Run before deployment to detect out-of-band changes.

text.en: Match each reference type to its use.
System database package reference
Same-database project reference
Different database, same server
Different server
Resolve references to master/msdb objects
Compose one database from multiple projects
Three-part names via a database SQLCMD variable
Four-part names via server and database SQLCMD variables

explanation.en: References make validation complete and let names vary by environment via SQLCMD variables.

example.en: [$(LinkedServer)].[$(ArchiveDb)].dbo.Orders

text.en: Where do you set SQLCMD variable values used by a project for a specific environment deployment?
In the publish profile or as /v: arguments to SqlPackage
In each table definition
In the master database
They can't be set

explanation.en: Publish profiles contain SqlCmdVariable values; SqlPackage also accepts /v:Name=Value overrides — handy in pipelines.

example.en: sqlpackage /Action:Publish … /v:SalesDb=SalesProd

text.en: Which statement about building SQL projects in CI agents (e.g. GitHub-hosted Linux runners) is true?
SDK-style projects build with the .NET SDK on Linux, Windows or macOS without SQL Server installed
They require Visual Studio on a Windows agent
They need a running SQL Server to build
They can't run in CI

explanation.en: Cross-platform builds are a headline benefit of Microsoft.Build.Sql. Original projects needed Windows/.NET Framework tooling.

example.en: GitHub Actions: actions/setup-dotnet then dotnet build.

text.en: Answer Yes or No about publish behavior.
Publish can deploy to Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, SQL Server and Fabric SQL database.
Publish always drops objects not in the project by default.
The Script action lets humans review changes before applying them.

explanation.en: SQL projects support the SQL Server/Azure SQL/Fabric family. DropObjectsNotInSource is false by default. Script output enables review/approval workflows.

example.en: Review deploy.sql in the PR; publish after approval.

text.en: A post-deployment script adds a row with INSERT … VALUES every time and duplicates appear after each deployment. What's the fix?
Make it idempotent with IF NOT EXISTS or MERGE
Deploy less often
Move it to pre-deployment
Disable the post-deployment script

explanation.en: Deployment scripts run on every publish, so they must be safe to re-run.

example.en: IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Settings WHERE [Key] = 'Theme') INSERT …

text.en: Production has security objects (users, role memberships) managed by the DBA team, not in the project. Publish with DropObjectsNotInSource = true would remove them. What's the safe configuration?
Keep DropObjectsNotInSource but exclude object types such as users, logins, role memberships and permissions (DoNotDropObjectTypes / ExcludeObjectTypes)
Accept the drops
Grant sysadmin to the pipeline
Disable the database's permissions

explanation.en: Publish options can exclude object types from drops/comparison so shared ownership works. The other options cause outages or excessive privilege.

example.en: /p:DoNotDropObjectTypes=Users;Logins;RoleMembership;Permissions

text.en: Complete the project file header for an SDK-style project targeting Azure SQL Database.
Microsoft.Build.Sql
Microsoft.NET.Sdk
Microsoft.Data.SqlClient
DSP
TargetFramework
OutputType

explanation.en: Microsoft.Build.Sql is the SQL project SDK; DSP sets the target platform (database schema provider). TargetFramework/OutputType are .NET app properties.

example.en: Other DSPs exist for SQL Server versions and Fabric SQL database.

text.en: Which statement about SQLCLR objects in SDK-style projects is correct?
They're supported but the project must build with .NET Framework
They're fully supported on .NET 8 builds
They're automatically converted to T-SQL
They're deleted during conversion

explanation.en: SQLCLR is the documented exception: projects containing it require .NET Framework to build, though the resulting dacpac deploys with SqlPackage on .NET.

example.en: Consider replacing SQLCLR with native features (e.g. REGEXP functions) to modernize.

text.en: Match each problem to the project feature that addresses it.
Column rename loses data on deploy
Lookup rows differ between environments
Build fails on new syntax
Need to review changes before applying
Refactor log (rename refactoring)
Idempotent post-deployment MERGE
Correct target platform (DSP)
SqlPackage Script / DeployReport

explanation.en: Four frequent SQL project issues and their built-in solutions.

example.en: These features make declarative deployments safe and repeatable.
